'''Junichiro Kono''' is a professor in the Departments of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Physics and Astronomy, and Materials Science and NanoEngineering, at [[Rice University]]. Since 2024, he is the director of the Smalley-Curl Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Junichiro Kono to lead Rice University's Smalley-Curl Institute - Energy Capital |url=https://energycapitalhtx.com/junichiro-kono-rice-university-smalley-curl-institute |access-date=2025-03-18 |website=energycapitalhtx.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Junichiro Kono received his B.S. and M.S. degrees in applied physics from the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1990 and 1992, respectively, and completed his Ph.D. in physics from the State University of New York at Buffalo in 1995. He was a postdoctoral research associate in condensed matter physics at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara|University of California Santa Barbara]] from 1995-1997, and the W. W. Hansen Experimental Physics Laboratory Fellow in the Department of Physics at [[Stanford University]] from 1997-2000. He joined the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering of [[Rice University]] in 2000 as an assistant professor and was promoted to associate professor in 2005 and to professor in 2009. He is currently a professor in the departments of electrical & computer engineering, physics & astronomy, and materials science & nanoengineering at Rice University.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eceweb.rice.edu/junichiro-kono|title=Junichiro Kono {{!}} Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE)|publisher=Rice University|accessdate=2018-06-19}}</ref> His research focuses on optical studies of condensed matter systems and photonic applications of nanosystems, including semiconductor nanostructures and carbon-based nanomaterials.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://kono.rice.edu/research/|title=Research {{!}} Junichiro Kono Laboratory|website=kono.rice.edu|access-date=2018-06-19}}</ref> He has made a number of pioneering contributions to the diverse fields of semiconductor optics, terahertz spectroscopy and devices, ultrafast and quantum optics, and condensed matter physics.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=http://kono.rice.edu/kono-bio/publications/|title=Publications {{!}} Junichiro Kono Laboratory|website=kono.rice.edu|accessdate=2018-06-19}}</ref> In 2009 he was named a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/units/dcmp/fellowship/index.cfm?year=|title=APS Fellowship|website=www.aps.org|access-date=2018-06-19}}</ref> and, in 2015, he was elected a Fellow of the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.rice.edu/2014/12/04/kono-named-optical-society-fellow/|title=Kono named Optical Society fellow|website=Rice University|date=2014-12-04|accessdate=2018-06-19}}</ref>
